newsitem.title: USA: Cattle reporting, meat shipping plan in US Senate.
newsitem.headline: Cattle reporting, meat shipping plan in US Senate.

text.p: Legislation to allow interstate shipment of state-inspected meat and to require more public information about so-called captive cattle supplies was introduced Monday by Senator Larry Pressler.
Pressler, South Dakota Republican, offered the plan in the U.S. Senate as an amendment to a funding bill for the Interior Department. A vote was not expected until Tuesday afternoon.

The amendment would define captive supplies as livestock acquired by packers at least seven days before slaughter under a standing purchase agreement, forward contract or packer ownership, feeding and financing.
The Agriculture Department would be required to report annually on the volume of cattle slaughtered through captive supplies including data on regional and local markets.
USDA would be required to make public, within 24 hours, of information received on sales involving captive supplies.
On state-inspected meat, USDA would be directed to allow interstate shipment -- now banned -- if a state's inspection program was at least as good as the federal system.
The amendment also would require meat to carry a country of origin label if it was graded and give the Food and Drug Administration more flexibility in licensing animal drugs.
